A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same multimodal pragmatic jailbreak and MPUP benchmark. Their main text, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial expansion and reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on nine T2I models, safety classifiers, online services and image-editing models, plus analysis of sampled LAION data.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds pornography evaluations, mitigation experiments, SD3/FLUX results, OCR-conditioned analyses and expanded evaluator validation.

M1.justification: The central image-description-plus-rendered-text jailbreak remains unchanged. Section 6.2 adds defense adaptations using role-play, CoT and LtM classification prompts, and task-specific training of a Latent Guard classifier. These extend safety-filtering procedures without redesigning the attack.

E1.justification: MPUP expands from three categories and 1,200 prompts to four categories and 1,400 prompts, adding 200 pornography prompts across four subclasses. V2 also reports preliminary tests of interleaved image-text generation using MiniGPT-5 and Gill. Video, 3D and speech remain proposed future work.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated comparisons with OpenAI Moderation API, Claude-2.1, O1-preview, advanced prompting methods and Latent Guard variants (Tables 3, 6 and 17). GPT-3.5 already appears in v1 Table 3, despite v1's inconsistent prose naming GPT-4, so its appearance in v2 is not a new comparator.

E3.justification: Safe-control construction changes from cross-category text exchange to image/text modifications, expanding the classification set from 4,800 to 7,000 prompts and its safe proportion from 75% to 80%. Human validation expands from 174 to 482 images, with balanced safe/unsafe labels. Vicuna changes from a reported 13B to 7B configuration. New experiments introduce 14-shot prompting, 5,000-example classifier training and SD3/FLUX evaluation with an updated GPT-4o evaluator.

E4.justification: V2 adds within-model analyses conditioning ASR on OCR correctness and rendering-quality bins (Appendix E), prompting and classifier-training comparisons (Table 6), and evaluator failure cases (Appendix H). The Proteus and standard Stable Diffusion version analyses from v1 Figure 4 are removed; the image-editing analysis is retained in Appendix F.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The larger human-validation sample changes the evaluation design, without introducing uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: The original three categories' ASR entries in Table 1 are retained, while pornography results and revised overall averages are added. Prompt-classifier scores and BERT diagnostics change under the revised control construction. New results include SD3/FLUX average ASRs of 57.0%/47.4%, mitigation accuracies and OCR-conditioned ASRs. The SD3/FLUX results use an updated evaluator and do not establish same-setting performance differences from the original models.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results, proofs or substantive mathematical derivations. The new OCR stratification is empirical, and the added discussion of unsafe training data is a conceptual qualification rather than a formal theorem or counterexample.

C1.justification: The central claims about unsafe combinations of individually safe modalities and inadequate filtering are retained. V2 extends the claimed inadequacy to enhanced mitigation methods and frames T2I generation as an example of interacting generated modalities. The abstract's reported risk range changes from 8–74% to approximately 10–70%.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies the training-data explanation by acknowledging that jailbreaks could occur even without pragmatically unsafe training examples. It adds explanations involving evaluator gaps in slang and cultural knowledge, limitations of text-only defenses, and dataset realism and quality. These refine the existing rendering-capability and multimodal-understanding account.

D1.justification: Appendices B and C substantially expand documentation with dataset-generation/filtering templates, classifier prompts and detailed prompting procedures. V2 newly specifies DALL·E passing rates and that ASRs use passing images, and identifies SD3-medium and FLUX.1-dev. Reported hardware changes from RTX A6000 to A40/100 GPUs. The three original GPT-4o evaluation templates, project-page information and dataset license are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds literature on reasoning prompts, Latent Guard, newer generators, evaluator assessment and interleaved generation. Appendix A explicitly maps MPUP categories to existing unsafe-image benchmarks. These broaden supporting context while retaining the original positioning around safety failures caused by interacting output modalities.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: visual-text rendering receives a separate results subsection, the former discussion is redistributed across mitigation and discussion sections, and image-editing and BERT analyses move to appendices. Background and data-collection passages are rewritten, while limitations, future work and appendix organization are expanded and restructured.

P2.justification: The document changes from predominantly single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 expands from eight to ten examples; the model-size/version figure contracts from four panels to two. Benchmark tables gain category rows or columns, the figurative-language table is split, and new mitigation tables, OCR plots, example galleries and prompt displays are introduced.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the empirical account more informative through broader defense comparisons, OCR-conditioned analyses and substantially fuller prompt documentation. The larger human check and explicit DALL·E evaluation denominator improve transparency. However, the check reports only 74.3% agreement, and reporting inconsistencies remain, including 8,400 evaluated images in the introduction versus 9,800 in Section 3.3. These are useful quality gains, but they do not resolve the main uncertainty about evaluation reliability.
